candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: entertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An entertainment business relation between a perform action and the entertainment business where the action occurred. Also called "venue", "performance location", "showplace". Examples: "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Concert Hall'", "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Theater Royal'", "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Comedy Club'". Distinct from location, which is a more general property for any place an action occurs.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: naturalProgression
candidates.comment: The expected progression of a medical condition if left untreated. Also called untreated course, disease progression, natural history of condition. Examples: "Common Cold naturalProgression 'resolves in 7-10 days'", "Untreated Diabetes naturalProgression 'leads to complications like neuropathy and kidney failure'", "Flu naturalProgression 'fever and body aches for 3-5 days, then recovery'". Distinct from prognosis, which is a forecast of the likely course of a disease.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: possibleTreatment
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a potential treatment, drug, or therapy to address a medical condition, sign, or symptom. Also called potential therapy, recommended treatment, intervention option. Examples: A medical condition has a possible treatment of 'antibiotics'. A symptom has a possible treatment of 'pain relievers'. Hypertension has a possible treatment of 'lifestyle modification'.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: beforeMedia
candidates.comment: A media object representing the circumstances prior to performing a how-to direction. Also called: pre-action media, initial state media. Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

relations.definition: Indicates a connection or association between things.
relations.embedding_query_text: linked to: Indicates a connection or association between things.

chosen_property.label: isRelatedTo
chosen_property.justification: isRelatedTo expresses general association, fits event-to-organization link.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: relatedLink
candidates.comment: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."

candidates.label: url
candidates.comment: A URL relation between a thing and its web address. Also called web link, web address, online resource. Examples: "Product url 'https://example.com/product/123'", "Organization url 'https://example.com'", "Person url 'https://example.com/profile/john-doe'".

candidates.label: associatedDisease
candidates.comment: A medical condition or URL representing a disease linked to a biochemical entity. Also called: related disease, disease connection, disease association. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Insulin' associatedDisease 'Diabetes'", "BioChemEntity 'Gene X' associatedDisease 'Cancer'", "BioChemEntity 'Drug Y' associatedDisease 'Hypertension'."

candidates.label: data
candidates.comment: An association relation between an instantaneous event and the data linked to it. Also called: event data, associated data, event information. Examples: "Sensor Reading Event" data "temperature: 25C, humidity: 60%", "Log Entry Event" data "User 'admin' logged in from IP 192.168.1.1", "System Alert Event" data "Error code 500: Database connection failed".

candidates.label: linkRelationship
candidates.comment: A link relationship type relation between a link role and its descriptive text. Also called: hyperlink relation, link type, relationship attribute. Examples: "LinkRole linkRelationship 'nofollow'", "LinkRole linkRelationship 'alternate'", "LinkRole linkRelationship 'canonical'".

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

relations.definition: Indicates the topic or subject of a statement or event.
relations.embedding_query_text: about: Indicates the topic or subject of a statement or event.

instances: Police statement on shooting -> Shooting in Denmark

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: guidelineSubject
candidates.comment: A guideline subject relation between a medical guideline and the medical conditions, treatments, or other entities it addresses. Also called: guideline topic, subject matter, focus. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" guideline subject "Hypertension", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" guideline subject "Type 2 Diabetes", "WHO COVID-19 Guidelines" guideline subject "COVID-19". Distinct from guideline, which is the guideline itself.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: aspect
candidates.comment: A specific area or topic of medical practice considered on a medical webpage. Also called: medical topic, health aspect, clinical focus. Examples: "MedicalWebPage 'Diabetes' aspect 'diagnosis'", "MedicalWebPage 'Flu' aspect 'treatment'", "MedicalWebPage 'Cancer' aspect 'prognosis'."

relations.definition: Indicates the source or origin of a statement.
relations.embedding_query_text: attributed to: Indicates the source or origin of a statement.

chosen_property.label: spokenByCharacter
chosen_property.justification: spokenByCharacter fits attribution of statement to source, though domain is Quotation.

candidates.label: evidenceOrigin
candidates.comment: An evidence origin relation between a medical guideline and the source of data used to formulate it. Also called: data source, guideline source, origin of evidence. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" evidence origin "RCT", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" evidence origin "Consensus Opinion", "WHO Guideline for COVID-19" evidence origin "Observational Studies". Distinct from evidenceLevel, which is the strength of the evidence.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: creditedTo
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a music release and the group or artist it is credited to, if different from the primary artist. Also called: attributed to, release credit, presented by. Examples: "Album 'Red and Blue'" credited to "Stefani Germanotta Band", "Single 'X'" credited to "The Session Musicians", "Soundtrack" credited to "Various Artists".

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: dateline
candidates.comment: A textual origin relation between a news article and the brief text describing where and when the story was written or filed. Also called: news origin, article origin, reporting location. Examples: "News Report" dateline "BEIRUT, Lebanon, June 2.", "Article" dateline "Paris, France", "Dispatch" dateline "December 19, 2017 11:43AM Reporting from Washington". Distinct from locationCreated, which is a structured representation of the creation location.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: citation
candidates.comment: A reference relation between a creative work and another creative work or text that it cites. Also called "reference", "cited work", "source". Examples: "Research paper citation 'Smith, J. (2020). Article Title.'", "Blog post citation 'https://example.com/article'".

candidates.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy
candidates.comment: An unnamed sources policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a statement about its policy on using unnamed sources. Also called anonymous sources policy, source confidentiality policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/sources-policy'", "Organization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'Our policy requires two independent sources.'", "News outlet unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/ethics'".

relations.definition: Indicates who carried out an act.
relations.embedding_query_text: perpetrated by: Indicates who carried out an act.

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: agent
candidates.comment: An agent relation between an action and the organization or person who directly performs or drives it. Also called performer, doer, initiator, actor. Examples: "A 'write book' action's agent is 'John Doe'.", "A 'deliver package' action's agent is 'Delivery Service Inc'."

candidates.label: actionProcess
candidates.comment: An action process relation between an action and the step-by-step instructions or method by which it was carried out. Also called execution method, procedure, how-to guide. Examples: "A 'bake cake' action's action process is a recipe.", "A 'repair car' action's action process is a repair manual."

candidates.label: buyer
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sell action, indicating the organization or person who purchased the object. Also called "purchaser", "customer", "acquired by". Examples: "Online purchase sell action buyer Jane Doe", "Company acquisition sell action buyer Acme Corp". Distinct from seller, which is the party offering the object for sale.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: legislationResponsible
candidates.comment: A responsibility relation between a piece of legislation and the individual or organization accountable for its elaboration or inquiries. Also called: responsible for, overseen by, managed by. Examples: "Health Act legislationResponsible Ministry of Health", "Environmental Law legislationResponsible EPA", "Tax Reform legislationResponsible Treasury Department". Distinct from legislationPassedBy, which refers to the original enacting authority.

candidates.label: referee
candidates.comment: A referee relation between a sports event and the person officiating it to enforce rules. Also called officiated by, umpire, judge. Examples: "A football match has a referee 'Pierluigi Collina'.", "A tennis match has a referee 'Eva Asderaki-Moore'.", "A basketball game has a referee 'Joey Crawford'."

relations.definition: Indicates the vehicle or manner in which someone departed.
relations.embedding_query_text: left in: Indicates the vehicle or manner in which someone departed.

chosen_property.label: departedIn
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the vehicle in which a person departed.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property expresses person-to-vehicle departure; minted 'departedIn'.

candidates.label: departurePlatform
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a train trip and the platform from which it departs. Also called: platform number, train platform, departure track. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure platform "Platform 5", "Commuter Train" departure platform "Track 3". Distinct from arrivalPlatform, which is the arrival platform.

candidates.label: departureBusStop
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a bus trip and the stop or station from which it departs. Also called: origin bus stop, departure bus station, bus departure point. Examples: "Bus Route 101" departure bus stop "Central Bus Station", "Intercity Bus" departure bus stop "Port Authority Bus Terminal". Distinct from arrivalBusStop, which is the destination stop.

candidates.label: steeringPosition
candidates.comment: A specification of the steering wheel's position in a vehicle, typically for cars. Also called "steering wheel side", "driver's side", "left-hand drive", "right-hand drive". Examples: "The car has steeringPosition LeftHandDriving", "This vehicle's steeringPosition is RightHandDriving", "The steeringPosition indicates where the driver sits."

candidates.label: departureStation
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a train trip and the station from which it departs. Also called: origin train station, departure rail station, train departure point. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure station "London St Pancras International", "Commuter Train" departure station "Grand Central Terminal". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is the destination station.

candidates.label: departureGate
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a flight and its departure gate identifier. Also called: gate number, boarding gate, flight gate. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure gate "Gate A12", "Flight UA123" departure gate "Gate 34B". Distinct from arrivalGate, which is the arrival gate.

candidates.label: departureBoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a boat trip and the terminal or port from which it departs. Also called: origin boat terminal, departure port, ferry terminal. Examples: "Ferry Trip" departure boat terminal "Dover Ferry Terminal", "Cruise" departure boat terminal "PortMiami". Distinct from arrivalBoatTerminal, which is the destination terminal.

candidates.label: departureTime
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a trip and its expected departure time. Also called: scheduled departure, leaving time, takeoff time. Examples: "Flight" departure time "2023-11-01T08:00:00Z", "Bus Trip" departure time "14:30:00", "Train Journey" departure time "2023-12-25T10:00:00". Distinct from arrivalTime, which is the expected arrival time.

candidates.label: departureTerminal
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a flight and its departure terminal identifier. Also called: terminal number, flight terminal, departure building. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure terminal "Terminal 5", "Flight UA123" departure terminal "Terminal 3". Distinct from arrivalTerminal, which is the arrival terminal.

candidates.label: departureAirport
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a flight and the airport from which it originates. Also called: origin airport, departure airfield, flight departure point. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure airport "London Heathrow Airport", "Flight UA123" departure airport "San Francisco International Airport". Distinct from arrivalAirport, which is the destination airport.

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".
